# Phase 0 — Asset Pipeline and Licensing

Status: complete, awaiting approval

---

## 1. The governing constraint

**No anatomical artwork ships with this repository, and none can be generated by an
assistant into a releasable state.**

That is not caution for its own sake. A plausible-looking illustration with subtly wrong
attachment, origin, or fibre orientation teaches a nursing student something false and does
it confidently. The cost of a wrong anatomical image is higher than the cost of a missing one.

Therefore:

- Art is **commissioned** or **explicitly licensed**, by a human, with a recorded licence.
- The repository ships **structure and pipeline**, not pictures.
- Developer builds may use **provisional placeholder geometry**, clearly watermarked, which
  is blocked from release by a build flag and by validator rules.

---

## 2. What is needed

| Asset category | Count (v1) | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Anterior base figure | 1 | Not supplied |
| Posterior base figure | 1 | Not supplied |
| Anterior muscle layer, one named group per structure | 12 | Not supplied |
| Posterior muscle layer, one named group per structure | 8 | Not supplied |
| Labels layer (anterior, posterior) | 2 | Not supplied |
| App icons (180/192/512/1024, maskable) | 5 | Design task, no anatomy content |
| UI icon set | ~14 | Small, purpose-built, in-house |
| Interface sounds | 0–3 | Optional; app is fully usable with none |
| Fonts | 1 family | See §7 |

Targets are the 12 anterior and 8 posterior structures listed in §3. The count is a
curriculum proposal requiring reviewer sign-off, not a fixed scope.

---

## 3. Proposed curriculum (requires reviewer sign-off)

This is a **teaching-scope proposal**, not approved medical content. It is the brief for the
commission brief, not a claim.

### Anterior view

| Region | Structure | Note for reviewer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Head & neck | Frontalis | Confirm teaching granularity for an introductory level |
| Head & neck | Sternocleidomastoid | Bilateral; confirm laterality handling |
| Shoulder | Deltoid | Region shared with posterior — confirm single vs paired entries |
| Thorax | Pectoralis major | Large, low-difficulty target |
| Thorax | Serratus anterior | Partly obscured by pectoralis major in anterior view; **verify selectability** |
| Upper limb | Biceps brachii | Introductory anchor |
| Abdomen | Rectus abdominis | Distinct segmentation; good early target |
| Abdomen | External oblique | Adjacent to rectus abdominis — **disambiguation required** |
| Lower limb | Rectus femoris | Anterior thigh |
| Lower limb | Vastus lateralis | Shares a boundary with rectus femoris — **disambiguation required** |
| Lower limb | Vastus medialis | Small teardrop shape — **likely needs magnifier or isolate mode** |
| Lower limb | Tibialis anterior | Anterior lower leg, good contrast |

### Posterior view

| Region | Structure | Note for reviewer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shoulder / back | Trapezius | Large, introductory |
| Shoulder | Deltoid | Posterior aspect — clarify whether one structure spans both views |
| Upper limb | Triceps brachii | Posterior arm |
| Back | Latissimus dorsi | Large; overlaps trapezius lower border — **disambiguation required** |
| Back | Erector spinae | **Only if visually represented accurately**; otherwise exclude from v1 |
| Lower limb | Gluteus maximus | Large, introductory |
| Lower limb | Hamstring group | Include as group, or exclude — a group alongside individual muscles violates LD-3's granularity rule |
| Lower limb | Gastrocnemius | Two heads; decide whether each head is separately selectable |
| Lower limb | Soleus | **Only if** its layer relationship is explained by an explicit layer mode |

**Three flags above are genuine curriculum problems, not formatting notes.** Each is resolved
by a reviewer decision, not by picking whichever is easier to draw:

1. Serratus anterior is partly covered by pectoralis major in anterior view. If it is not
   fairly selectable, it is removed from v1 rather than given a hitbox that reaches through
   the pectoralis.
2. Erector spinae and soleus are layer-dependent. Asking a learner to identify a partly hidden
   muscle on a superficial illustration is a trap. They ship only with an explicit, explained
   layer mode, or not at all in v1.
3. Hamstring group alongside individual muscles in one pool violates the granularity rule.
   Either all-levels are individual or the pool excludes the group.

Recommendation to the reviewer: cut to 10 anterior and 6 posterior, all clearly visible and
individually selectable, and add depth in v1.1 once the loop is proven. A smaller honest set
teaches more than a larger compromised one.

---

## 4. Illustration specification (commission brief)

Delivered to the illustrator as a written specification.

### Canvas and geometry

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| ViewBox | `0 0 1000 2200` for both views |
| Midline | `x = 500` |
| Ground contact | `y = 2200` |
| Top of head | `y = 0` |
| Pose | Neutral anatomical: arms slightly abducted ~10°, palms forward in anterior view, feet hip-width |
| Scale | Identical across both views so spatial memory transfers |
| Aspect | 1 : 2.2, portrait-friendly inside landscape |

Both views must use the same proportions and the same ground line. If the posterior figure is
drawn at a different height, cross-view learning breaks silently.

### Layer separation

Five separate deliverables per view, so the app can combine them independently:

1. `*-base.svg` — silhouette only, no muscle detail, non-interactive
2. `*-muscles.svg` — one `<g>` per structure, named by `visual_id`
3. `*-states.svg` — none; state styling is CSS-driven in the app
4. `*-labels.svg` — text layer, positions only, hidden during quiz
5. `*-hit.svg` — none; hit strokes are duplicated from muscle paths in code

Deliver **layered SVG or a vector master that exports clean SVG**. Not PDF. Not a flattened
raster. Raster is acceptable only for a photographic or gradient reference, never for the
anatomy itself.

### Naming contract

One `<g>` per structure, with `id` equal to the `visual_id` and both data attributes present:

```xml
<g id="muscular.anterior.biceps_brachii.surface"
   data-structure-id="muscular.biceps_brachii"
   data-visual-id="muscular.anterior.biceps_brachii.surface">
```

This contract is non-negotiable. An asset whose IDs do not match `visual-mappings.json`
fails content validation and cannot ship. See §6.

### Anatomical requirements

- Fibre direction must be visually correct and consistent with the actual muscle.
- Origins and insertions must not be simplified into positions that imply a wrong action.
- Superficial muscles only, unless a structure ships with an explicit layer mode.
- Left/right mirroring must not break `laterality`. A structure declared `bilateral` appears
  once as a mapping and is drawn on both sides; a structure declared `right` only is drawn
  and labelled on the correct side.
- No sexualisation, no exaggeration, no heroic posing, no dramatic lighting, no sci-fi
  hologram treatment. Clinical neutrality.
- Respectful and clinically appropriate, and free of any suggestion of dissection,
  injury, or pathology. This is a healthy-body teaching illustration.
- Labels must use standard anatomical terminology, spelled consistently with
  `canonical_name` in the content pack.

### Accessibility of the art

Muscle fill must contrast against the base silhouette and against its neighbours by **at least
3:1**. Two adjacent muscles that a learner must distinguish may not rely on hue alone —
separation by outline weight or subtle value difference is required, and the board adds a
non-colour cue on selection.

---

## 5. Licensing rules

Non-negotiable, and machine-enforced where possible.

### Prohibited

- Never scrape, screenshot, trace, vectorise, or extract anatomy from commercial anatomy
  products, textbooks, or atlases without explicit written permission.
- Never treat "free to view" as "free to reuse".
- Never embed a commercial product's models, screenshots, illustrations, or data without a
  licence permitting exactly the intended use, in exactly the intended distribution channel.
- Never use AI-generated anatomy as a release asset without qualified expert review of the
  specific image, and never as a silent default.
- Never assert a licence that has not been read and recorded.

### Preferred order

1. Commissioned original art, owned by the project (clearest, most defensible).
2. Open licence with compatible terms (CC0, CC-BY).
3. Open licence with share-alike or non-commercial terms (only if those obligations are
   compatible with the intended distribution — **and they usually are not** for a product
   intended for classroom use).
4. Licensed commercial asset with written permission covering web delivery, modification,
   and redistribution.

### The share-alike trap

CC-BY-SA artwork used in the app makes derivative assets share-alike obligations apply to the
modified artwork. A muscle layer edited to match `visual_id` is a derivative. If the project
cannot accept that obligation, CC-BY-SA is not an option. Same for CC-BY-NC if any intended
use is commercial. Decide this **before** commissioning, not after delivery.

### Recorded per asset

`asset_id`, `file_path`, `asset_type`, `associated_system_id`, `associated_structure_id`,
`source_creator`, `source_url_or_reference`, `license`, `attribution_requirement`,
`modification_notes`, `medical_review_status`, `reviewer`, `review_date`, `content_version`.

Every one of those fields is required before an asset can be referenced by a published
structure.

### Release gate

`npm run build` fails when any asset referenced by a published structure has:

- `license: 'UNSET'`
- `license: 'proprietary_restricted'`
- `medical_review_status !== 'approved'`
- missing attribution where the licence requires it

---

## 6. SVG optimisation rules

Optimisation is required for the performance budget and is also where art gets broken. The
rules are enforced by a test, not by discipline.

**Must preserve:**

- `id` attributes
- `data-structure-id` and `data-visual-id`
- `data-selection-priority`
- `<title>` and `<desc>`

**Must strip:**

- `<script>` elements
- Event handler attributes (`onclick`, `onload`, and any other `on*`)
- `xlink:href` / `href` pointing outside the file
- `<foreignObject>`
- Unused `<defs>`, `<filter>`, and `<mask>` — filters are a performance risk and a
  correctness risk
- Editor metadata (`inkscape:*`, `sodipodi:*`, `sketch:*`, Illustrator blocks)
- Embedded raster images

**Must not introduce:**

- Path coordinate rounding that shifts geometry more than ~0.5 user units
- `transform` folding that breaks the layer-group contract
- Auto-merged paths, which would destroy per-structure separation

**Pipeline:**

```
master (layered SVG from illustrator)
  → strip script/handlers/external refs        (script, unit-tested)
  → strip editor metadata and unused defs     (svgo, pinned preset)
  → preserve-id check                         (test: fail if any visual_id lost)
  → path precision 2 decimals                 (svgo)
  → gzip
```

`svgo` is pinned to a specific version and its preset is committed to the repo, because a
minor version bump can silently change path output and break geometry.

---

## 7. Typography

**One family, licensed for web embedding.**

Recommended: **Source Sans 3** (SIL Open Font License 1.1) or **Inter**
(SIL OFL 1.1). Both permit self-hosting, embedding, and redistribution with the licence
file retained. Bundle `.woff2` only, `font-display: swap`, preloaded for the single weight
used in headings.

Avoid: AI-default display typefaces, condensed faces at small sizes, and any face whose
licence forbids web embedding. The licence file ships in `public/licenses/`.

---

## 8. Icons and sounds

### Icons

~14 purpose-built 24×24 icons, 1.5–2 px stroke, `currentColor`, drawn in-house so there is no
third-party icon licence question: menu, close, info, reset, zoom in, zoom out, check,
cross, reveal (eye), hint, skip, chevron, book, settings.

Rules: icons always accompany a text label, or carry an explicit `aria-label`. An icon-only
button with no accessible name does not ship. No icon set chosen for its default look.

### Sounds

Optional, default **off**, and the app is fully usable with sound disabled — that is an
accessibility requirement, not a preference. At most three short, non-jarring cues: correct,
incorrect, session complete. No sound on every tap. No stingers that startle. Soft-limit
concurrency to three so overlapping cues cannot stack.

---

## 9. Provisional art (development only)

To build and test the interaction model before art exists:

- Simple geometric SVG shapes in `src/assets/anatomy/muscular/*/`, clearly named
  `provisional-*`.
- Filenames carry `provisional` so they cannot be mistaken for deliverable art.
- `PROVISIONAL_ART` build flag adds a persistent, non-dismissible notice:
  "Provisional placeholder illustration — not anatomically accurate."
- `ALLOW_DRAFT_CONTENT` is on in development only.
- Release builds fail while either flag is on.

Provisional art is for engineering. It is never for a screenshot in a report, never for a
demo to a reviewer as evidence of content quality, and never in a build shown to a learner.

---

## 10. `AssetManifestEntry` template

`src/data/manifests/asset-manifest.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "./asset-manifest.schema.json",
  "content_version": "1.0.0",
  "entries": [
    {
      "asset_id": "asset.anatomy.muscular.anterior.muscles",
      "file_path": "/assets/anatomy/muscular/anterior/anterior-muscles.svg",
      "asset_type": "svg",

      "associated_system_id": "muscular",
      "associated_structure_id": null,

      "source_creator": "FILL — illustrator or rights holder",
      "source_url_or_reference": "FILL — licence URL or signed contract reference",
      "license": "UNSET",
      "attribution_requirement": null,
      "modification_notes": "FILL — e.g. 'paths renumbered to visual_id contract'",

      "medical_review_status": "provisional",
      "reviewer": null,
      "review_date": null,

      "content_version": "1.0.0"
    },

    {
      "asset_id": "asset.anatomy.muscular.anterior.base",
      "file_path": "/assets/anatomy/muscular/anterior/anterior-base.svg",
      "asset_type": "svg",
      "associated_system_id": "muscular",
      "associated_structure_id": null,
      "source_creator": "FILL",
      "source_url_or_reference": "FILL",
      "license": "UNSET",
      "attribution_requirement": null,
      "modification_notes": null,
      "medical_review_status": "provisional",
      "reviewer": null,
      "review_date": null,
      "content_version": "1.0.0"
    }
  ]
}
```

One entry per file, not per structure. A single muscle layer SVG is one asset with one
licence; the per-structure mapping lives in `visual-mappings.json`. Licensing is a property of
the file, medical approval is a property of the mapping.

---

## 11. Credits screen

Required for release. Data comes from `asset-manifest.json` and `sources.json`, rendered
verbatim — never hand-written, so credits cannot drift from the manifest.

Contents:

- App name, version, build id
- Anatomy illustration credits: creator, licence name, licence URL, attribution text
- Required modification notices
- Educational source list: title, author, edition, year, reviewer, review date
- Font licence
- Explicit statement of what the app is and is not

Copy:

> Muscle Atlas is an educational study aid. It does not provide diagnosis, treatment advice,
> or clinical decision support, and it does not replace anatomy laboratory instruction or
> professional education. Illustrations are simplified teaching figures and do not represent
> the full complexity of human anatomy.

---

## 12. Acceptance criteria (art and licensing)

- [ ] Every shipped asset has a real licence recorded, read, and verified for the intended use.
- [ ] No `UNSET` licence in any release build.
- [ ] No `proprietary_restricted` asset in any release build.
- [ ] Every asset referenced by a published structure is `medical_review_status: 'approved'`.
- [ ] SVG optimisation preserves all `visual_id`, `structure_id`, and `data-*` attributes.
- [ ] No `<script>`, event handler, `foreignObject`, or external reference survives optimisation.
- [ ] Illustrator master is layered SVG with per-structure named groups.
- [ ] Anterior and posterior figures share viewBox, scale, and ground line.
- [ ] Adjacent muscles are distinguishable without relying on hue alone.
- [ ] Every published structure has `min_fair_target_px` recorded and a fairness affordance
      where the target is under 44 px.
- [ ] Credits screen renders from the manifest and matches it exactly.
- [ ] Provisional art and draft content are impossible to reach in a release build.
